title: What's New: Coding Business Central Agents with AI Development Toolkit

chapters.title: Getting Task Results and Agent Sessions

features.name: Agent Type Definition
features.description: A blueprint for agents that defines default settings and identity through enum extensions for agent metadata provider and Copilot capability.

features.name: Agent Factory Interface
features.description: Defines default settings for agents including first time setup page, copilot capability binding, default profile, and default permissions.

features.name: Agent Metadata Interface
features.description: Defines runtime behavior of agents including summary page, message review page, agent initials, and context-specific settings.

features.name: Task Execution Interface
features.description: Controls message processing behavior including input/output message validation, user intervention suggestions, and context-specific settings.

features.name: Message Validation API
features.description: Allows implementing relevance checks, adding warnings on input messages, and modifying output messages to add signatures.

features.name: Agent Instances
features.description: Agents are modeled as instances which are also users in Business Central, each keeping their own permissions, profile, user settings, and instructions.

features.name: Agent Setup Page
features.description: A configuration dialog page type used to create and configure agent instances, with standard agent setup component and custom settings.
caveats: Users design their own setup pages for custom agents

features.name: Agent Setup Codeunit
features.description: Allows creating and managing instances of agents and tracking them in custom tables with agent configuration.

features.name: Programmatic Agent Creation
features.description: Agents can be created dynamically through the agent codeunit, tied to actions or workflows, within user sessions.
caveats: Must be in a user session

features.name: Agent Instructions
features.description: Instructions can be loaded at any time during agent lifetime, typically loaded during agent creation from a resource.

features.name: Agent KPI Pages
features.description: Display important metrics about an agent when users hover over the agent's avatar, using card part pages.

features.name: Tasks API
features.description: Automates task creation for agent instances using agent task and builder codeunits to build tasks and messages.

features.name: Task and Message Model
features.description: Tasks are units of work bound to agent instances with input messages providing context, and agents create output messages. Multi-turn interactions are supported.

features.name: Message Attachments
features.description: Ability to add attachments such as PDF documents to messages, with text extraction performed by the agent.

features.name: Multi-turn Agent Interactions
features.description: Supports continuing discussions with agents through multiple input and output messages, simulating email threads or continuous discussions.

features.name: External ID for Messages
features.description: Field on messages allowing tying messages to concepts like email threads for finding and continuing them.

features.name: Agent Task Triggering
features.description: Tasks can be triggered by embedding them in Business Central as page actions or through events and processes in AL.

features.name: Agent Task Codeunit Management
features.description: Provides functions to manage agents and tasks including stopping tasks, restarting them, and other management operations.

features.name: Task Result Polling
features.description: Wait for task results via polling using the agent task record status field to check completion state.
caveats: Good for unit testing and non-production scenarios

features.name: Agent Session Events
features.description: Create events that only fire in agent sessions, allowing code to trigger after agent actions in the UI.

features.name: Is Agent Session Procedure
features.description: Provided by agent session codeunit to determine if current session is an agent session.

features.name: Exposing Agents via API
features.description: Expose agents to other apps by creating public functions in a codeunit that other apps can call, while maintaining security boundaries.
caveats: By default agents are isolated to own app for security

quotes.text: Today we will see how we can use the APIs provided in Business Central to code our own agents.
quotes.why_it_matters: Sets the core objective of the session: teaching developers to build agents using Business Central APIs.

quotes.text: In Business Central, agents are modeled via instances which are also users in Business Central.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies the fundamental architectural model: agents are instances and users, establishing how agents are created and managed.

quotes.text: you will need to make your own table to track your own instances. It needs to be a table that has the user security
quotes.why_it_matters: Specifies a key technical requirement for agent implementation - using user security ID as primary key for instance tracking.

quotes.text: For tasks, you can imagine them as units of work for the agent. They are bound to a specific agent instance.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the task model that developers use to assign work to agents.

quotes.text: Multi-turn interactions are also supported because you can insert multiple input messages, and the agent might answer multiple times.
quotes.why_it_matters: Confirms multi-turn conversation capability enabling complex agent interactions.

quotes.text: By default, the AL API only supports interacting with agents defined in your own app.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes default security boundary where agents are isolated to their own app.
